notes:
Topline: building realtime personalized shopping assistant + product reranker. Extremely latency-sensitive: 30-80ms target for interactive flows; if not, UX drops. Cost constraints: unit economics tight on long tail — want to reduce per-token cost via batching/quantization/caching.

Recent quotes: CTO said 'we can't accept >80ms median in checkout assistant' and VP Product: 'cost must be predictable; surprise token spend kills the use case'.

POC details: running two buckets - 1) Hosted API quick POC (small scale) to validate correctness and A/B quality vs in-house; 2) Dedicated/VPC for latency isolation and predictable throughput. SE recommended: start with int8 variant + persistent KV cache across sessions to reduce repeated context compute. Also exploring per-customer prefix caching for product catalogs.

Benchmarks so far: baseline (in-house) p50=42ms p95=160ms for 128-token chat; Redwood hosted POC run p50=35ms p95=140ms but with KV cold-start spikes to 250ms. Team wants guidance on autoscaling/batching knobs to flatten p95.

Security: must integrate with KMS for key ownership, SSO/SAML for operator access, and maintain audit logs for transactions. Data residency: primary US region, EU for EU customers.

Next steps: 1) SE-run controlled perf sweep (batch sizes, KV warm strategies, quant profiles) 2) produce a one-page recommended config + estimated unit economics 3) legal/VPC contract review and KMS proof-of-concept.
